notes.title: Version 1.3 Released!
notes.notes:
I'm back!

We've got a new update dropping today! This episode's not black or white, it's sort of in... The Gradient.

[h2]Full Change List:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added force zones, or gravitational gradients, or whatever I feel like calling them this week. If you put something in them, it gets pushed in one direction. They may be wacky and conservation-law-defying, but they're still gravity. They'll accelerate a giant iron sphere just as much as a speck of dust.
[*] Added 20 new levels using the new mechanic and exploring its many uses. We've got 140 levels now!
[/list]

notes.title: Version 1.2 Released!
notes.notes:
Introducing The Zone of Time! In this sixth episode on the level select screen, you'll need to keep the balls in the target zones for long enough to trigger them, or shoot through the bad target zones fast enough to avoid triggering them. It's all about timing. Hence the name.

[h3]Full change list:[/h3]

[list]
[*] The aforementioned target zones
[*] 20 new levels, bringing the total to 120!
[*] The version number is now 1.2
[/list]

notes.title: Version 1.1 Released!
notes.notes:
Version 1.1 of NBody Gravitation has been released! This update contains a new episode with 20 more levels, bringing the total up into the triple digits.

[h2]Additions:[/h2]
A new episode: The Target Mine! Back in the olden days, targets were all stationary and didn't react to gravity at all. Our new targetsteroids fix that, and we got 20 new levels out of this mechanic.

I thought the same 60-second loop might get a bit old after 100 levels, so this update also contains new in-level music, set to play on episodes 2 and 5. It has a trombone.

[h2]Changes:[/h2]
The title screen was changed to say "NBody Gravitation" instead of simply "NBody". Originally, the game's name was just "NBody", but this was changed in the last few days before version 1.0 released, after all the marketing materials were finished. I found out that an unrelated game called "n-body", with a hyphen, already exists on Steam, and I wanted to avoid confusion.

Antimatter star balls now properly invert their colors instead of turning gray.

The antimatter annihilation effect now has a purplish tint.

notes.title: NBody has been released!
notes.notes:
Well, I did it. I made another game. As the title, subtitle, and summary said, it released today. 

NBody is a puzzle game about gravity. Plenty of other people have made n-body gravity sandboxes, but this is a full-fledged quasi-educational puzzle game. It's got 80 levels at launch, so expect to spend at least a few hours with it!
